# Susan Baker

## Overview

- **Gender:** Female  <sub>[v4 c18 P52](../source/v04-c18.md#nw-v04-c18-p0052), [v4 c22 P5](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0005)</sub>
- **Status:** Unmarried  <sub>[v4 c18 P52](../source/v04-c18.md#nw-v04-c18-p0052), [v4 c22 P5](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0005)</sub>
- **Origin:** The Glen  <sub>[v4 c18 P52](../source/v04-c18.md#nw-v04-c18-p0052)</sub>
- **Role:** Maid-of-all-work for Dr. Gilbert Blythe and Anne Blythe  <sub>[v4 c18 P52](../source/v04-c18.md#nw-v04-c18-p0052), [v4 c19 P0](../source/v04-c19.md#nw-v04-c19-p0000)</sub>

## Appearance

Susan is a grim-faced, elderly spinster who considers herself no beauty, though as good-looking as most married women. When walking long distances, she puffs heavily.

_Sources: [v4 c18 P52](../source/v04-c18.md#nw-v04-c18-p0052), [v4 c22 P5](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0005), [v4 c38 P35](../source/v04-c38.md#nw-v04-c38-p0035)_

## Personality

Susan is a kind-hearted, industrious, and fiercely loyal handmaiden who takes immense pride in her household duties and cooking. Though grim-faced and prone to dark, resigned proverbs about human trouble, she prefers to cheer people up rather than weep with them. She holds a deep, affectionate devotion toward Anne and her child, often declaring herself to be 'at the helm.' She is fond of men, admits candidly that she enjoys seeing a well-looking man, and holds strong opinions about cellars, pantries, and ears.

_Sources: [v4 c18 P52](../source/v04-c18.md#nw-v04-c18-p0052), [v4 c19 P0](../source/v04-c19.md#nw-v04-c19-p0000), [v4 c19 P10](../source/v04-c19.md#nw-v04-c19-p0010), [v4 c22 P5](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0005), [v4 c23 P5](../source/v04-c23.md#nw-v04-c23-p0005), [v4 c36 P21](../source/v04-c36.md#nw-v04-c36-p0021), [v4 c40 P47](../source/v04-c40.md#nw-v04-c40-p0047), [v4 c40 P49](../source/v04-c40.md#nw-v04-c40-p0049)_

## History

Susan Baker was installed as the maid-of-all-work for Gilbert and Anne Blythe at their little house of dreams in Four Winds. She grew to worship 'young Mrs. Doctor' with intense fervor and took complete charge of the kitchen and household management. During Anne's dangerous labor and the loss of her first baby, Joy, Susan wept bitterly for her mistress's grief and lovingly cared for her during her recovery. She remained employed at the little house through the birth of Little Jem, guarding the child fiercely and taking charge whenever Anne was away. When her sister Matilda broke her leg, Susan temporarily left to care for her, but returned as soon as possible to resume her duties. When Gilbert bought the Morgan house at the Glen, Susan rejoiced over the larger quarters and superior cellar, ultimately helping the family pack up and move from the little house.

_Sources: [v4 c18 P52](../source/v04-c18.md#nw-v04-c18-p0052), [v4 c19 P0](../source/v04-c19.md#nw-v04-c19-p0000), [v4 c19 P5](../source/v04-c19.md#nw-v04-c19-p0005), [v4 c19 P17](../source/v04-c19.md#nw-v04-c19-p0017), [v4 c19 P18](../source/v04-c19.md#nw-v04-c19-p0018), [v4 c22 P0](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0000), [v4 c35 P18](../source/v04-c35.md#nw-v04-c35-p0018), [v4 c36 P19](../source/v04-c36.md#nw-v04-c36-p0019), [v4 c38 P35](../source/v04-c38.md#nw-v04-c38-p0035), [v4 c40 P43](../source/v04-c40.md#nw-v04-c40-p0043), [v4 c40 P47](../source/v04-c40.md#nw-v04-c40-p0047), [v4 c40 P58](../source/v04-c40.md#nw-v04-c40-p0058)_

## Quotes

> Now for breakfast. I am of the opinion that we will all be glad of a bite and sup. You tell young Mrs. Doctor not to worry about a single thing—Susan is at the helm. You tell her just to think of her baby.  <sub>[v4 c19 P10](../source/v04-c19.md#nw-v04-c19-p0010)</sub>

> You just take it easy, Mrs. Doctor, dear. Have a good time and do not worry about the pantry. Susan is at the helm. There is no use in keeping a dog and doing your own barking. I am going to take your breakfast up to you every morning.  <sub>[v4 c22 P3](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0003)</sub>

> Is it not funny nobody ever asked me to marry him, Mrs. Doctor, dear? I am no beauty, but I am as good-looking as most of the married women you see. But I never had a beau. What do you suppose is the reason?  <sub>[v4 c22 P5](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0005)</sub>

> Well, I never could see but that my bread rose just as light when Grits were in as when they were not. And if any party, Mrs. Doctor, dear, will make it rain before the week is out, and save our kitchen garden from entire ruination, that is the party Susan will vote for.  <sub>[v4 c35 P17](../source/v04-c35.md#nw-v04-c35-p0017)</sub>

> Well, I never was much hand for weeping, Mrs. Doctor, dear. I would rather fall to and cheer people up than weep with them. Now, do not you cry and spoil your pretty eyes. This house is very well and has served your turn, but it is high time you had a better.  <sub>[v4 c40 P49](../source/v04-c40.md#nw-v04-c40-p0049)</sub>
